old_title: Live: Sharks lose star with Roosters on top in semifinal
new_title: Roosters power into prelim as Sharks insist they are not in rebuild mode
old_text:
Fri, 11 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Rabbitohs 10, Knights 20
live
NRL live: Sydney Roosters vs Cronulla Sharks semifinal live scores and updates
Nicho Hynes cops an early head knock, ruling him out of Cronulla's sudden-death semifinal against the Sydney Roosters.
Hynes was concussed while trying to make a tackle in just the second minute of the game, moments before the Roosters ended their opening set of the game with a try.
Follow all the action in our live blog below, check out all the stats in the full ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio coverage.
Submit a comment or question
Live updates
NRL semifinal live: Sydney Roosters vs Cronulla Sharks
New: Filters
Choose what information you see below by using filters
Key Event
HALF-TIME: Roosters lead battered and bruised Cronulla 18-10
The Sharks make it through the final few minutes of the half without sustaining any more damage to their personnel or on the scoreboard, but this next 40 minutes is going to be brutal for them.
No Nicho Hynes since the second minute and now missing Mawene Hiroti to a knee injury, Cronulla needs an almighty effort to hold off this rollicking Roosters outfit.
If the Tricolours can sort out their discipline, they should have some luck out there. Already we've seen some frailty in defence from the Sharks.
36' Roosters get away with one
Niwhai Puru shapes for a high kick for a flying Ronaldo Mulitalo, who's blatantly taken out by Reece Robson off the ball, but the referee ignores the Sharks' cries.
DCE hits back in slo-mo
Well that all happened very slowly off a couple of set restarts.
The Roosters play it under the posts and Daly Cherry-Evans gets it one off the ruck.
Cam McInnes races up to try to stop a rampaging Spencer Leniu, but he never sees it and DCE is left one on one with Will Kennedy, just stepping inside the fullback and reaching out to score.
Key Event
BANG BANG! The Sharks go back to back!!
Blayke Brailey shreds the Roosters through the middle and sends Sifa Talakai flying upfield.
Braydon Trindall wastes no time capitalising on the quick play the ball, wrapping around to the left and hitting a flying Ronaldo Mulitalo to crash and roll over.
Trindall manages to convert this one and the Sharks are down by just two points with 14 minutes left in this half.
"I've got goosebumps," says 2016 Clive Churchill medallist Luke Lewis on ABC Sport.
Key Event
Against all odds, the Sharks are in!
Cronulla spins it right and Braydon Trindall bravely digs into the line before flinging a ball over the top to Sione Katoa, who looks boxed but he bursts between Billy Smith and Daniel Tupou to slam the ball down.
Hynes is out, right centre Mawene Hiroti has stayed off since that bat-back, and Trindall was down holding the shoulder after stumbling after throwing that pass.
Trindall is having to kick goals with Hynes out, and he can't convert from out on the right sideline.
19' Roosters argue the toss to no avail
Braydon Trindall's chip kick is batted back as he dives over the dead ball line. Billy Smith, standing out of bounds, catches the ball, which I'd have thought means the bat-back is dead akin to a winger putting his foot in touch to mark a kick and make it out on the full, but referee Adam Gee disagrees.
Key Event
13' Nicho Hynes is ruled out
The Sharks have lost their halfback for the game after he failed his head injury assessment.
Craig Fitzgibbon has a real reshuffle now, as Niwhai Puru comes onto the field for Hynes.
Key Event
Daniel Tupou flies high for another try!
Billy Smith gets the Roosters rolling with an early left side shift and Daniel Tupou finishes it off as he sails over a frankly hapless Sione Katoa to mark Hugo Savala's cross-field kick and ground the ball.
9' The Sharks are over, but can't get it down
Jesse Colquhoun charges onto a pass and comes within a whisker of grounding the ball.
He comes up millimetres short, and it's a good thing too, because he would've been called for a double movement if he had grounded it.
Instead it's a play the ball ... and they knock it on anyway as Braydon Trindall is forced to reach for a pass with that injured right arm and can't hold on.
The Roosters hang on after a prolonged assault on their line.
Key Event
The Roosters are in and Hynes is down!
The Roosters storm up the field through Salesi Foketi and spin it right quickly, where Daly Cherry-Evans holds up the pass for big Lindsay Collins to crash over.
Meanwhile, in back play, Sharks halfback Nicho Hynes is coming off for an HIA.
He copped Foketi's hip to the head, which led to the line break. Hynes was left dazed on the ground for a while and he's straight off the field for a head injury assessment.
1' First test for Braydon Trindall's shoulder
The Sharks pivot launches a long kick and Victor Radley hits his injured right arm as he strikes it.
He's up and OK, giving a bit of lip to Radley.
I think it'll be a kick on the other side of the field that will cause issues if his injured right shoulder hits the ground unprotected.
Key Event
1' The Roosters kick off
Braydon Trindall marks, and Addin Fonua-Blake barrels into the mighty Roosters forward pack.
Who you got?
Crowd watch
We were left with about 47,000 empty seats across three games in Sydney in the first week of finals, so it will be interesting to see what sort of crowd we get tonight.
The Sharks fans proved last week with their 17,429-strong crowd that they don't love travelling to the Sydney Football Stadium, and the Roosters aren't renowned for having the most passionate fanbase in Australian sport.
It's never a good look when the NRL can't fill a 42,000-seat stadium for a final, especially when the AFL is packing out far bigger arenas on the same weekend.
Key Event
Broncos thump Knights to move into NRLW prelims
It took less then a minute for the Broncos to score the opening try against the Knights in their NRLW semifinal.
And on and on it went like that.
The Broncos ended up scoring at just under a point a minute in a 34-0 opening half, with Romy Teitzel doubling up and former Newcastle halfback Jesse Southwell slotting 5/6 conversions.
Brisbane will face local rivals the Titans on the Gold Coast on Sunday, September 27.
Key Event
LATE MAIL: Hiroti returns for the Sharks
The Sharks have centre Mawene Hiroti back in the starting line-up this week, with Riley Jones dropping to the bench.
Cronulla five-eighth Braydon Trindall will continue to play through the pain of his injured shoulder.
For the Roosters, Angus Crichton is back on the bench.
Key Event
It's NRL semifinal night!
Hello and welcome to ABC Sport's live coverage of tonight's NRL semifinal clash between the Sydney Roosters and Cronulla Sharks.
It's a contest between two perennial finalists for whom a loss at this stage will be nowhere near good enough.
The tension is ratcheting up as we approach a 7:50pm AEST kick-off at the Sydney Football Stadium.

Fri, 11 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Rabbitohs 10, Knights 20
Sydney Roosters thump Cronulla Sharks 46-10 in NRL semifinal
The Sydney Roosters are 80 minutes away from their first NRL grand final in seven years after fighting past Cronulla in a 46-10 semifinal win.
Trent Robinson's men will play the Dolphins in a preliminary final after being made to work for victory against the Sharks at Sydney Football Stadium.
Halfback Daly Cherry-Evans was placed on report for tripping Cronulla's Teig Wilton on Saturday and, aside from the fitness of Sam Walker, is likely to be the only question mark heading into next Friday's meeting with the Dolphins.
Queensland number seven Walker underwent ankle surgery less than a month ago but coach Trent Robinson said the team is "pretty confident" he will be back to face the Dolphins.
"He hasn't trained with us yet but he's had really good progressions," Robinson said.
Just as everything fell into place for the Roosters, who also welcomed back Angus Crichton from a long injury lay-off on Saturday, just about everything fell apart for Cronulla.
Halfback Nicho Hynes failed a head injury assessment after copping a bang en route to Lindsay Collins' second-minute opening try.
And then centre Mawene Hiroti went off with a knee injury after 20 minutes after crashing over the dead-ball line.
It was little wonder the Roosters put a depleted Sharks outfit to the sword, piling on 24 points in the final half an hour.
Cronulla is now one of just two teams in the NRL era to reach five straight finals series without making a grand final, and has not been returned to the last game of the season despite making the top eight in nine of 10 seasons since.
"We've been up for five years now with the same group of guys and a good portion of those are leaving," Sharks coach Craig Fitzgibbon said.
Cameron McInnes, Sione Katoa, Siosifa Talakai, Jesse Ramien and Mawene Hiroti are some of the core members of the team on their way out, but Fitzgibbon said it would not be a complete rebuild for the club.
"Everyone thinks we need a reset or rebuild; we'll just keep going, we've got some guys ready to go," he said.
"We won't be going anywhere."
Look back at all the action in our live blog below and check out all the stats in the full ScoreCentre.

We'll leave you there
Make sure you return tomorrow for the Warriors-Knights blockbuster from a packed Eden Park.
Until next time, enjoy all the sport.
Roosters 'pretty confident' Sam Walker will be back next week
Roosters coach Trent Robinson says it was "a good day", with he and James Tedesco reserving special praise for Daly Cherry-Evans, who missed a chance to ice the qualifying final against the Panthers last week.
"He's got plenty of experience, he's nailed those many time but he's gone through his hardship as well. He was our leader tonight," captain Tedesco says.
"Chez doesn't hold onto things, he goes out and executes."
But the good news is Sam Walker is a good chance of coming back next week.
"Pretty confident from what we've seen. He hasn't trained with us yet but he's had really good progressions."
And they'll need his attacking flair against the red-hot Phins.
The Sharks 'won't be going anywhere'
Cronulla coach Craig Fitzgibbon says the second-half blowout was basically the price of the fight his team showed in the first 40 minutes.
"What possibly could've went wrong went wrong and then it was like a 'hang on' energy for the rest of the game."
He's asked about Daly Cherry-Evans not being sin-binned after being penalised for a trip on Teig Wilton in a try-scoring position, and implies the Sharks have been dudded for "six straight weeks", but stops short of really saying anything.
Cronulla is one of just two teams in the NRL era to reach five straight finals series without making a grand final, and haven't been back despite making the top eight in nine of 10 seasons since the 2016 premiership.
"We've been up for five years now with the same group of guys and a good portion of those are leaving. I'm forever grateful for their service, punching above their weight for a long time now."
Cameron McInnes, Sione Katoa, Siosifa Talakai, Jesse Ramien and Mawene Hiroti are all leaving the club, but Fitzgibbon says it won't be a complete rebuild for the club.
"Everyone thinks we need a reset or rebuild; we'll just keep going, we've got some guys ready to go. We won't be going anywhere."
Cameron McInnes agrees.
"There won't be any dip. I really believe the best is ahead for the club."
Key Event
When is the Dolphins-Roosters preliminary final?
The Dolphins and Roosters will face off for a spot in the NRL grand final on Friday, September 25, from 7:50pm AEST at Brisbane's Lang Park.
Sharks great signs off
Cameron McInnes has played his last NRL game, for now at least.
And he says the overarching feeling right now is frustration, rather than sadness.
"We had all intentions to come out tonight and play the way we wanted to, but from the start things didn't go our way," he tells ABC Sport.
"It just got a bit quick on us and then we fought our way back in, but the ending's probably the most frustrating part."
For those of you keeping score, the Roosters scored 22 of their 46 points in the last 19 minutes of the game.
The Sharks weren't helped by the injuries, but things really unravelled as the fatigue set in.
"Things move quickly, you've got to get on with it, it's not ideal. It all adds up. They were just too good."
Key Event
FULL-TIME: The Roosters storm into the preliminary finals
It ends up a dominant 46-10 victory for the Sydney Roosters, who progress to a preliminary final against the Dolphins up in Brisbane.
With Nicho Hynes out since the second minute with a concussion, Mawene Hiroti out for the majority of the game and Braydon Trindall carrying a serious shoulder injury, the Roosters honestly should have put this game away earlier, but they really stormed home in this one.
78' Getting silly now from the Roosters
They're doing what they want, but Daly Cherry-Evans's kick across the field shows it's not all roses as it flies into touch in the in-goal.
Marky Mark gets another one
The Cronulla defence has nothing left and the Roosters are toying with them as DCE steps past a few in the middle, flicks it to Hugo Savala, who finds Tedesco, to Toia.
He beats a man and grubbers through for himself, but the ball holds up to beat him and the Sharks. But of course Mark Nawaqanitawase is there to clean up with a gorgeous pick-up to score.
The Roosters are just having fun now
They're throwing the ball around and this time it's a lovely outside-in play from DCE to Siua Wong to James Tedesco, who bobbles as he reverses and spins through the defence to score.
Key Event
Rob Toia flies high and adds another for the Roosters
That will end this one as a contest as Rob Toia steams past the Sharks and outleaps Ronaldo Mulitalo to score a spectacular try.
Mark Nawaqanitawase is over for the Roosters
A lovely bit of interplay between Reece Robson, Victor Radley and Daly Cherry-Evans is beautifully summed up by a bullet-like long ball by DCE out to a flying Mark Nawaqanitawase to dive over on the right wing.
61' Billy Smith saves the day
Billy Burns hits the line hard and works to get his arms free. He offloads to Braydon Trindall 2 metres short of the line, but before he can secure it, Billy Smith arrives and knocks it loose.
60' Teig Wilton crosses dubiously, DCE on report
The Sharks back rower is adamant he's scored a bullocking try, but Adam Gee says no try because of a double movement.
Gee is correct, but before the double movement, Daly Cherry-Evans tripped him.
58' Sharks still a chance
The Roosters are pressing, but Rob Toia knocks on a high bullet pass by Daly Cherry-Evans.
The 14-point deficit feels like a lot, but with over 20 minutes left and the Roosters seemingly incapable of completing a set at the moment, Cronulla is still in the fight.
Mike called it
We must be due for a bit of Marky Mark magic...
- Mike
I think you might be the magic one, Mike.
Loading
Key Event
THAT IS MAGICAL FOOTY!!
The Roosters score an absolute worldie through Connor Watson under the posts, but it won't surprise you to know the magic started with Mark Nawaqanitawase out on the right wing.
The right-side shift found the dynamic winger, who again looked destined for the sideline, but he once again flings a perfectly directed behind-the-back pass to Rob Toia.
He offloads to James Tedesco, who offloads to no-one. But Siua Wong scoops the bouncing ball off his toes and fires it left to Hugo Savala. He finds Watson, who looks off numbers to the left, beats Sifa Talakai and KL Iro with footwork and bumps off Blayke Brailey to crash over for a ridiculous try.
50' Rob Toia is crunched
The right-side shift calls for quick hands and Rob Toia obliges with a bat-on to Mark Nawaqanitawase. But the Roosters centre cops a huge jamming tackle into his ribs by Ronaldo Mulitalo for his trouble.
48' Another bad kick by Trindall
Braydon Trindall's playmaking has won the Sharks more than a few games, but this time it's brought them unstuck as a shorter cross-field kick is again too deep and Rob Toia marks well above his head as Ronaldo Mulitalo arrives.
47' The Roosters can't get out of their own way
Another error, this time by Nat Butcher, who just fumbles as he prepares for a hit-up, and the Sharks feed a scrum 25 metres out.
The Roosters should be dominating this game and they can't stop making errors.
